title: The Golden Age: Beginner Hypertrophy
author: Duncan
desc:
To train beginners to:
1. Learn how to push themselves in the gym and realize that quality matters more than quantity
2. Build coordination and skill on key movement types to properly engage the target muscle (compounds AND isolations. Free weight AND Machines)
3. Make the gym an enjoyable habit instead of a chore
4. Dissolve any social anxiety around the gym by gaining confidence in fitness experience
5. Educate beginners to a degree where they become capable of  creating their own programs based on their goals

Here's an FAQ filled with topics I think are important for all beginners to know. Read before running this program
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1UVE0NqfoeSHVPKcBgFQFBniDCck67oDx24rczPErKWI/edit?usp=sharing

This program is meant to be run for approximately the first 3 months of a completely new trainee. However, as a beginner, you can keep milking this program dry for many more months. I don't make anything I wouldn't do personally. I would see gains running this exact same program.

The program is a 4x a week torso/limb split. That's a fancy way of saying chest, back, and shoulders one day then legs and arms the other day. A traditional upper lower is perfectly fine, but there's simply more muscles to stimulate in the upper body. Switching arms to leg day works because the arms already don't get a good stimulus from pushing and pulling exercises, so they will very likely be recovered. If your biceps are sore from your back work, I have bad news for you-your form is probably bad. Also, by rewarding leg work with fun arm work, it will make sure you don't become a leg day skipper.

One set of days must be done back to back. The other days CAN be done back to back but do not have to be done back to back. This is to allow flexibility in schedule, as it's likely beginners will at some point be unable to commit to a session for any given reason.

This program is built for time efficiency with a selection of antagonistic supersets so the time commitment to the gym feels less daunting for beginners. If access to equipment is harder to come by in your gym, just split up the superset and do the exercises individually. Not a big deal, it will just take a bit longer.

Rep ranges aren't a huge deal. Anywhere between 5-20 is going to work about just as well if you train hard. The rep ranges in the program are suggestions, not rules.

Suggested days: Any combination works as long as the number of rest days in between are the same
M: Rest
T: Torso 1
W: Limb 1
Th: Rest
F: Rest
Sat: Torso 2
Sun: Limb 2

or

M: Rest
T: Torso 1
W: Rest
Th: Limb 1
F: Rest
Sat: Torso 2
Sun: Limb 2

ss.note: Mid-back focus. Round your shoulders and let your arms stretch as far forward as they'll go. Pull the bar toward your chest by squeezing your shoulder blades back
Keep the incline consistent and somewhere around 15-45 degrees. Stick your chest up the WHOLE TIME. While maintaining a proud chest, bring the dumbbells to the shoulders or if you can, biceps
Maintain and arched back and pull the cable to your chest. Imagine driving your elbows into your sides. At the top, let your arms get stretched upwards as far as they'll go
Set the cable to where your hand is when standing up regularly. You can go behind the body or in front of the body. Most importantly, keep is consistent. Imagine "sweeping" the weight out

ex.note: Push your butt back as far as it will go while keeping your spine relatively neutral. A little knee bend is perfectly fine, but use as little knee bend as you can to get to good depth.
Place your feet at a comfortable width and angle toward the bottom of the machine to bias the quads. Go as low as you can without your butt coming off the seat (may need to adjust the range)

ss.note: Keep your elbows close to your sides and drive the bar into your body as opposed to straight downward. Keep a slight knee bend for balance and bracing. It's okay to let your elbows come up at the top
At the bottom of the rep, your elbow should be straight. You may need to take a step back from the cable machine in order for this to happen
Arch your back and bring your chest to the bar. Grab the bar with your palms down. If you can't do weighted, np. Put weight as 0 and track bw or assisted reps with the notes function.

Stick your chest out by imagining your try to press a button with your pecs. Close=more balanced, wide=more pec. If going forward hurts your shoulders, try facing backwards. Dw about the weighted part
Upper back focus. Set the chest pad so that you can fully extend you arms. Reach as far as you can, letting the weight stretch your back. Squeeze your shoulder blades back as you pull
Depending on your height, you may bottom out. Sit on a yoga mat/block to increase the range of motion

ex.note: Use the handle that allows you to feel your rear delts more. Imagine trying to "paint" as much area as you can by sweeping the weight outward
Bar should rest on top of your upper traps. Take a comfortable stance that allows you to go as low as you possibly can while staying balanced. Toe angle and feet width will vary for each person

Maintain and arched back and pull the cable to your chest. Imagine driving your elbows into your sides. At the top, let your arms get stretched upwards as far as they'll go
Set the cable to where your hand is when standing up regularly. You can go behind the body or in front of the body. Most importantly, keep is consistent. Imagine "sweeping" the weight out

ex.note: Push your butt back as far as it will go while keeping your spine relatively neutral. A little knee bend is perfectly fine, but use as little knee bend as you can to get to good depth.
Place your feet at a comfortable width and angle toward the bottom of the machine to bias the quads. Go as low as you can without your butt coming off the seat (may need to adjust the range)

ss.note: Keep your elbows close to your sides and drive the bar into your body as opposed to straight downward. Keep a slight knee bend for balance and bracing. It's okay to let your elbows come up at the top
At the bottom of the rep, your elbow should be straight. You may need to take a step back from the cable machine in order for this to happen
Arch your back and bring your chest to the bar. Grab the bar with your palms down. If you can't do weighted, np. Put weight as 0 and track bw or assisted reps with the notes function.

Stick your chest out by imagining your try to press a button with your pecs. Close=more balanced, wide=more pec. If going forward hurts your shoulders, try facing backwards. Dw about the weighted part
Upper back focus. Set the chest pad so that you can fully extend you arms. Reach as far as you can, letting the weight stretch your back. Squeeze your shoulder blades back as you pull
Depending on your height, you may bottom out. Sit on a yoga mat/block to increase the range of motion

ex.note: Use the handle that allows you to feel your rear delts more. Imagine trying to "paint" as much area as you can by sweeping the weight outward
Bar should rest on top of your upper traps. Take a comfortable stance that allows you to go as low as you possibly can while staying balanced. Toe angle and feet width will vary for each person

ss.note: Lean forward and hug the handles for a crazy hamstring stretch and very stable exercise. Keep going until the weight doesn't move at all, not when you can't get to the bottom anymore
Lean the seat back as far as it will go. You can often get a handful of half reps once you can't reach the top on these as well
Turn around and use the back of the preacher curl pad to support your torso. Keep your elbows straight and up high as much as you can while still feeling comfortable
Fully extend your elbow so it's straight at the bottom. Digging your armpits into the pad may help you feel more supported. You won't hurt yourself on these unless you're stupid. Use control
